title: Maximum Ascending Subarray Sum
spaceBreakdown:
- int n: single integer → O(1)
- int maxSum: single integer → O(1)
- int curSum: single integer → O(1)
- int i (loop variable): single integer → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vector, returned int
approach: Scan the array once left to right, maintaining a running sum of the current strictly ascending subarray. When `nums[i] > nums[i-1]`, extend the current subarray by adding `nums[i]` to the running sum; otherwise, reset the running sum to `nums[i]` (starting a new subarray). Track the maximum running sum seen at every step. This is correct because every ascending subarray is a maximal chain of consecutive strictly-increasing pairs, and the running sum captures exactly the sum of the current chain.
hints:
When does the current ascending subarray end and a new one begin as you scan left to right?
A subarray is a contiguous sequence of numbers in an array.

Use a single-pass running sum: maintain `curSum` for the current ascending subarray, adding `nums[i]` when `nums[i] > nums[i-1]`, otherwise resetting `curSum` to `nums[i]`. In Example 1, after `[10,20,30]` gives `curSum = 60`, the pair `(30, 5)` breaks ascending order so `curSum` resets to `5`.

```
maxSum = nums[0]
curSum = nums[0]
for i = 1 to n-1:
    if nums[i] > nums[i-1]:
        curSum = curSum + nums[i]
    else:
        curSum = nums[i]
    maxSum = max(maxSum, curSum)
return maxSum
```

**Single element** - n = 1, the loop body never executes
`Input: nums = [42]` → `Expected: 42`
⚠️ Bug: initializing maxSum to 0 instead of nums[0] → returns 0

**All equal values** - no two consecutive elements are strictly increasing
`Input: nums = [7,7,7,7]` → `Expected: 7`
⚠️ Bug: using >= instead of > in the comparison → returns 28

**Descending array** - every element starts a new subarray
`Input: nums = [50,40,30,20,10]` → `Expected: 50`
⚠️ Bug: always adding nums[i] to curSum without checking ascending order → returns 150

**Peak before the end** - the maximum subarray is not the last one
`Input: nums = [10,20,30,5,10]` → `Expected: 60`
⚠️ Bug: returning curSum instead of maxSum → returns 15

followUps.q: What if the array can contain negative numbers?
followUps.a: The algorithm structure is unchanged - a single element is always a valid subarray, so initializing maxSum to nums[0] still works. When the ascending property breaks, curSum resets to the new element even if it is negative, but maxSum retains the best seen so far. TC: O(n), SC: O(1).

followUps.q: What if we need the maximum sum of a strictly increasing subsequence (not necessarily contiguous)?
followUps.a: Use dynamic programming where dp[i] is the maximum sum of an increasing subsequence ending at index i. For each i, scan all j < i with nums[j] < nums[i] and set dp[i] = max(dp[i], dp[j] + nums[i]). TC: O(n²), SC: O(n).

followUps.q: What if the array is streamed element-by-element and is too large to store in memory?
followUps.a: The current solution already processes elements one at a time and only needs the previous element, the running sum, and the maximum - three variables total. It handles streaming directly with no modification. TC: O(n), SC: O(1).
